Blair.feeling: Tense and muddled: my Pigeon and hug claims in earlier rounds didn't hold up, and Casey's sudden death has left the table split on who the Meowfia are.

Casey.feeling: Frustrating: my Hawk egg gave a clear read on Ellis, but I was silenced by a wink before I could finish the vote.

Drew.feeling: Confusing and contradictory: the Owl and Hawk reports point at Ellis, but Ellis's clean dawn and Blair's Tit claim don't line up, and Casey was winked just as the vote was forming.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and messy: the day has been full of conflicting visit stories, and I'm Meowfia with a Wink that just got used on Casey before the vote.

Finley.feeling: Tense and muddled: Casey was silenced before the vote, and the visit claims keep contradicting each other.

Alex.note: Casey's Hawk gain on Ellis is the only hard evidence, and Casey was probably Farm given the wink. I'll throw at Ellis with my lowest card.

Blair.note: Casey's Hawk egg makes Ellis likely Meowfia, possibly my partner, so I shouldn't help eggsecute Ellis. I'll throw one low card at Alex, who has been pushing the vote, to avoid feeding the Ellis throw.

Casey.note: I'm dead, so my throw doesn't count as a vote, but it still banks if Farm wins. I'll throw my lowest card at Ellis, the confirmed Meowfia.

Drew.note: My Owl read shows a Floofer and a Hawk visited Ellis, and Casey's Hawk egg confirms Ellis is Meowfia-linked. Throwing at Ellis with low cards, keeping high ones.

Ellis.note: Meowfia wins by eggsecuting a Farm player, so I'll throw my Wild at Finley, who has been pushing the vote against me. The Wild is worth 0, so it's the cheapest vote to risk.

Finley.note: Casey was winked, but Drew's Owl read and the Hawk egg still point at Ellis. I'll throw my wild W2 at Ellis, a vote that costs me nothing if we win.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey and Hugged rules were hard to track: a Floofer visit left no trace in my dawn report, so I couldn't tell whether a player had been hugged or simply not visited. Confused players also made the egg-count checks unreliable.
Alex.fun: Round 3 was tense: Casey, a Farm Hawk, pushed hard and then collapsed to a Wink mid-day, and the other players called the vote on Ellis, who was actually Meowfia.
Alex.change: I'd make dawn reports tell a player whether they were visited and by which animal type when that's safe to reveal, so Turkey and Floofer claims can be checked without guessing.
Alex.regret: In Round 2 I threw at Ellis, a Farm Turkey, while my Meowfia partner Blair was the one who got eggsecuted, so I helped the Farm side win. I should have pressed harder to protect Blair by pointing out Ellis's Turkey claim was true and Blair's visit story was the one to question, or thrown at Blair's accuser instead.

Blair.confusing: The Floofer's hug rules were hard to track: it wasn't clear whether a hug still counts as a visit for the Turkey and Owl reads. Confused dawn reports also made it hard to tell honest mistakes from lies.
Blair.fun: Watching the table pile onto Blair's shifting Pigeon, visit, and hug stories in round 2 was a tense, lively moment. The day discussion really felt like a social deduction game.
Blair.change: I'd make dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since hugs and confusion made it hard to separate lies from honest mistakes. Each nest change should also be easier to trace back to a specific visit.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I invented a Pigeon claim and then a visit story that didn't match the egg counts, which got me voted out. I should have stayed quiet and avoided making checkable claims that contradicted the nests.

Casey.confusing: Whether dead players' throws still count, and how the Meowfia team's throws work when a teammate is one of the targets. I wasn't sure whether throwing at a teammate could ever help, so I didn't know how to weigh it.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when Blair's Pigeon claim fell apart by egg count. I checked the Eagle's +1 against Finley's Falcon read and it made the whole table turn on Blair.
Casey.change: I'd make it clearer when a Wink is used and who it hits, since a dead player's vote was a surprise to me. I'd also show each player's role-group more openly so the Meowfia can coordinate.
Casey.regret: In round 1 as Meowfia, I threw a Wild at Alex, my own teammate, which helped eliminate them and cost my side the round. I should have thrown at a Farm player instead, or kept my card and stayed quiet.

Drew.confusing: The Owl and Floofer visit reports were hard to verify, since one visitor's hug or egg outcome was not visible to the target without a clear report. Being told a hug versus no visit made the day hard to sort out.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when Blair's Pigeon, visit, and hug stories kept collapsing one by one under questioning, and the table converged on the right throw.
Drew.change: I would make the dawn report clearer about hugs versus missed visits, so a Floofer's effect is easier to check against the target's own report.
Drew.regret: In Round 1 I threw only my Wild, which banked 0 points when a 1 would have banked 1, and I would throw my lowest real card instead.

Ellis.confusing: The dawn reports didn't make clear whether a hug or a Floofer visit shows up on your nest, which left me unsure whether Blair's and Drew's visit claims could be checked. Also, the Storyteller's note that Meowfia can't tell who is who made the Round 3 vote hard to read.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when Blair's Pigeon, visit, and hug stories fell apart one by one against the egg counts, and the table finally threw at them. Catching a liar with nest arithmetic felt satisfying.
Ellis.change: Spell out in the dawn report exactly what a hug, a Floofer visit, and a Turkey visit each do to the nest, so players can test claims without guessing.
Ellis.regret: In Round 3 I used my Wink on Casey, the Hawk whose egg count was correct, when Drew, the Owl, was also accurately reporting visits and was just as dangerous. I would wink at whichever accuser had the most reliable report, which was Drew's Owl read.

Finley.confusing: The rule for hugs was unclear: a Floofer's visit leaves no trace in the visited player's nest or dawn report, so a clean report can't rule out a visit. That made Ellis's "nobody visited me" impossible to test.
Finley.fun: Cross-checking the Falcon result against Casey's Eagle count in round 2 caught Blair's false Pigeon claim by the exact egg totals. Nest counts turned out to be real evidence.
Finley.change: Make dawn reports say when a player was hugged or visited by a Floofer, so a clean nest is clearly distinguishable from a hidden visit.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I accepted Alex's Owl story and leaned Farm, when Alex was the Floofer and Meowfia. I should have pressed Alex's visit claim harder and asked Drew to name the Falcon target before the vote.

review.title: Hugs and Silent Winks
review.headline: Ellis, a Farm leader, skated through three rounds and won by banking safely.
review.summary: Round 1 was thin: a Floofer hugged every visitor, a false Owl claim passed, and Alex still got eggsecuted. In round 2 Blair's Pigeon bluff broke against Casey's Eagle count and Meowfia lost. In round 3 Casey's Hawk egg and Drew's Owl read exposed Ellis, and his Wink killed the accuser but could not stop the vote. Ellis won on 18 mostly from one early 8-point bank and a final-round return of a Wild, not from deduction in the final standings.

rounds.recap: Alex (Floofer) hugged Casey. Three Farm players visited Alex and got nothing, and Alex then claimed Owl. The table accepted it for lack of any evidence. Votes were thin Wilds and low cards, and Alex was eggsecuted almost by accident, with Casey (Mouser) and Drew throwing at Alex while Blair and Finley split onto Drew.

Blair (Floofer) claimed Pigeon, but Casey's Eagle result showed her +1 came from only one visitor. Blair's claim collapsed, then shifted to a hug story. Everyone but Alex threw at Blair and she lost. Alex, the other Meowfia, knew Ellis was Farm and threw at him in vain.

Casey's Hawk egg and Drew's Owl read (Floofer and Hawk visited Ellis) pointed straight at Ellis. Ellis winked Casey mid-day, but Casey's claim had already landed and Finley's CAW ended the day. Ellis was eggsecuted, and Farm won.

highlights.text: Casey's Eagle +1 from Finley's single visit to Drew broke Blair's Pigeon claim and became a clean cross-check.
Casey's Hawk egg on Ellis and Drew's Owl list of Floofer and Hawk gave a two-source, near-certain read.
Ellis used his Wink on Casey mid-day, but the accusation was already spread across the table and the vote still hit him.
Three Farm players visiting a hugging Floofer all got nothing, and Alex's unverifiable Owl claim survived the day.

confusions.what: As Turkey he said nobody visited him, yet he was hugged. He and the table also argued that a visitor to a Turkey should show in Blair's nest, which ignores that a hugged Turkey does nothing.
Claimed Pigeon with a visit to Casey while her real visit was to Ellis, then said her report 'may have been confused', which she had no basis for.
Said Ellis would have been told he was hugged. She also said her Floofer visit was a 'hug' while Ellis's dawn showed no hug notice, and the rules do not say hugs are reported.
Said 'someone visited' Ellis to challenge the Turkey claim, but Alex's own Sphinx visit went to no one. He chose no target and learned Ellis's identity by role.
Said a Floofer visit would have left him hugged and visible in his dawn report. Hugs are not reported, so the objection was invalid.
Said Ellis's 'nobody visited' could not explain Casey's +1, which was a confused point since the Turkey was unrelated to Casey's egg.
Claimed Owl but said he learned animals that visited Casey; Casey's Mouser visited Drew, so there were none, and Alex then dodged naming them.

worked: Egg counts as public evidence: Casey's Eagle +1 vs Blair's Pigeon claim broke a bluff cleanly in round 2.
Hawk and Owl together in round 3 gave Farm two independent reads, which made the deduction feel earned.
The Wink creates a real choice: Ellis silenced the accuser mid-day, a dramatic beat even though it failed.
Throw sizes as a signal and a hidden-value bank gave real decisions, such as Ellis's 8-point win in round 1.
problems: Round 1 had almost no information: a Floofer hugging three visitors silenced the whole day, and a false Owl claim could not be tested. Consider telling hugged players they were hugged, or reporting visit counts.
Hugs are silent, which drove several bad arguments (rounds 2 and 3) about whether Ellis should have felt a hug. State plainly in the rules whether hugs are reported.
The score race is lopsided: Ellis's 8-point bank in round 1 decided the game, and later rounds barely threatened him. Add catch-up, or cap banked card value.
Meowfia don't know each other, and Alex (Sphinx) did the best Meowfia play by knowing a Farm role, yet it did not matter. Meowfia rarely have a viable plan, so they lost twice in a row.
Players mostly threw Wilds and low cards at the Farm consensus, so the vote carried little risk. The throw-and-bank incentive rarely made anyone choose between teammates and their own score.
